newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech crown jumps, helped by foreign buying.
newsitem.headline: Czech crown jumps, helped by foreign buying.

text.p: The Czech crown recovered some of its recent losses on Tuesday on foreign buying as the market cautiously awaited Wednesday's trade figures, dealers said.
Mid-afternoon the crown was at 26.816 to the dollar, 17.713 to the mark or 3.02 percent above the central bank's weighted mark/dollar basket, mainly on the strength of a large purchase.
It then eased toward a central bank fixing of 2.80 percent above that basket.
The crown opened the morning barely higher than two percent above parity of the mark/dollar basket, after the central bank's fixing at +2.61 percent on Monday.

"There was a huge Czech crown purchase coming through the whole morning from outside the Czech Republic, and this caused a lot of the participants on the market to be short (in crowns)," said Petr Korous at CSOB in Prague.
"This was a totally contrarian move," Korous added, saying it was not yet clear who was behind the large trade.

Korous said market sentiment was still mostly negative with the government getting battered by the opposition about recent problems of banks, amid calls for the dismissal of Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik.
The crown had been dropping since the middle of last week.

Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus and his Civic Democratic Party have refused to recall Kocarnik and have primarily blamed the Czech National Bank for lax supervision in the failure of Kreditni Banka a.s. and illiquidity at Agrobanka a.s..
Dealers said they expected crown buying to remain cautious as the market awaits the latest update on a widening trade deficit when August merchandise results are released on Wednesday morning.
Oto Otepka at Girocredit said the market would react negatively if Wednesday's results implied a trade deficit that surpassed 150 billion to 160 billion crowns for the entire year.
"If the projection of August figures exceeds this range, then the markets will get very cautious and probably sell Czech crowns," Otepka said.
A July deficit of 16.4 billion crowns put the trade gap at 85.3 billion crowns for the first seven months of the year.
